005package org.wpilib.math.estimator;
006
007/**
008 * This class estimates the input bias required to make the expected motor velocity match the actual
009 * velocity over one timestep.
010 *
011 * <p>Subtracting this input bias from the next control input will cancel it and eliminate
012 * steady-state error. This method of fixing steady-state error is superior to a pure integral
013 * controller because it only integrates for unmodeled disturbances, not during expected transient
014 * behavior while converging to a reference. This means there won't be overshoot during transients.
015 *
016 * <p>The feedforward gains passed to this class should match the ones used by the mechanism's
017 * feedforward. The estimator estimates the error in that feedforward model; if the gains differ,
018 * the difference shows up as input bias. In particular, errors in kV appear as an input bias
019 * proportional to velocity, and errors in kA appear as an input bias during acceleration. Logging
020 * the input bias estimate against velocity is a useful way to find these: a slope indicates kV
021 * error, and a sign flip on direction reversal indicates kS error.
022 */
023public class DCMotorBiasEstimator {
024  private final double m_ks;
025  private final double m_kg;
026
027  // Discrete velocity model
028  private final double m_A;
029  private final double m_B;
030
031  // Observer gains
032  private final double m_l1;
033  private final double m_l2;
034
035  // State estimate
036  private double m_velocity;
037  private double m_inputBias;
038
039  /**
040   * Constructs a DC motor bias estimator.
041   *
042   * <p>The model is
043   *
044   * <pre>
045   * a = −kV/kA·v + 1/kA·(u + d) − kS/kA·sgn(v) − kG/kA
046   * </pre>
047   *
048   * <p>where a is the acceleration, v is the velocity, u is the applied voltage, and d is the
049   * estimated input bias.
050   *
051   * <p>For an arm, whose gravity term depends on angle, pass zero for kG and subtract the gravity
052   * feedforward voltage from the voltage passed to {@link #calculate(double, double)} instead.
053   *
054   * @param ks The static gain in volts. This should match the feedforward's kS, or be zero if the
055   *     feedforward doesn't use one.
056   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts. This should match the feedforward's kG, or be zero if the
057   *     feedforward doesn't use one.
058   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(units/s). Must be non-negative.
059   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(units/s²). Must be non-negative. kV and kA can't both be
060   *     zero.
061   * @param timeConstant The approximate time in seconds for the input bias estimate to converge to
062   *     a new constant input bias. Larger values reject disturbances more slowly but react less to
063   *     model error and measurement noise. Must be positive.
064   * @param dt Nominal discretization timestep in seconds. Must be positive.
065   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the parameter constraints are violated.
066   */
067  public DCMotorBiasEstimator(
068      double ks, double kg, double kv, double ka, double timeConstant, double dt) {
069    if (kv < 0.0) {
070      throw new IllegalArgumentException("kv must be non-negative, got " + kv + "!");
071    }
072    if (ka < 0.0) {
073      throw new IllegalArgumentException("ka must be non-negative, got " + ka + "!");
074    }
075    if (kv == 0.0 && ka == 0.0) {
076      throw new IllegalArgumentException("kv and ka can't both be zero!");
077    }
078    if (timeConstant <= 0.0) {
079      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
080          "Time constant must be positive, got " + timeConstant + "!");
081    }
082    if (dt <= 0.0) {
083      throw new IllegalArgumentException("dt must be positive, got " + dt + "!");
084    }
085
086    m_ks = ks;
087    m_kg = kg;
088
089    // Discretize the velocity dynamics v' = −kV/kA v + 1/kA (u + d) with a
090    // zero-order hold. See wpimath/docs/SimpleMotorFeedforward.md for the
091    // derivation, including the kA = 0 and kV = 0 cases.
092    if (ka == 0.0) {
093      m_A = 0.0;
094      m_B = 1.0 / kv;
095    } else if (kv == 0.0) {
096      m_A = 1.0;
097      m_B = dt / ka;
098    } else {
099      // B_d = A⁻¹(eᴬᵀ − 1)B simplifies to (1 − A_d)/kV
100      double exponent = -kv / ka * dt;
101      m_A = Math.exp(exponent);
102      m_B = -Math.expm1(exponent) / kv;
103    }
104
105    // The augmented system is
106    //
107    //   xₖ₊₁ = Φxₖ + Γuₖ
108    //   yₖ = Cxₖ
109    //
110    // where
111    //
112    //   x = [v]  Φ = [A_d  B_d]  Γ = [B_d]  C = [1  0]
113    //       [d]      [ 0    1 ]      [ 0 ]
114    //
115    // The predictor-form observer is
116    //
117    //   x̂ₖ₊₁ = Φx̂ₖ + Γuₖ + L(yₖ − Cx̂ₖ)
118    //
119    // where L = [l₁  l₂]ᵀ. Subtracting it from the augmented system gives the
120    // estimation error dynamics
121    //
122    //   x̃ₖ₊₁ = (Φ − LC)x̃ₖ
123    //
124    // where x̃ = x − x̂ and
125    //
126    //   Φ − LC = [A_d − l₁  B_d]
127    //            [  −l₂      1 ]
128    //
129    // The error dynamics' poles are the roots of the characteristic polynomial
130    //
131    //   det(zI − (Φ − LC)) = det([z − A_d + l₁   −B_d ])
132    //                            ([    l₂       z − 1 ])
133    //                      = (z − A_d + l₁)(z − 1) + B_d l₂
134    //                      = z² − (1 + A_d − l₁)z + (A_d − l₁ + B_d l₂)
135    //
136    // Matching coefficients with the desired characteristic polynomial
137    //
138    //   (z − p_v)(z − p_d) = z² − (p_v + p_d)z + p_v p_d
139    //
140    // gives
141    //
142    //   1 + A_d − l₁ = p_v + p_d
143    //   A_d − l₁ + B_d l₂ = p_v p_d
144    //
145    // The first equation gives l₁. Substituting A_d − l₁ = p_v + p_d − 1 from
146    // the first equation into the second gives l₂.
147    //
148    //   l₁ = 1 + A_d − p_v − p_d
149    //   B_d l₂ = p_v p_d − p_v − p_d + 1
150    //   l₂ = (1 − p_v)(1 − p_d)/B_d
151    //
152    // The input bias pole p_d uses the given time constant. The velocity pole
153    // p_v is placed 5x faster so the input bias estimate's convergence time is
154    // dominated by its own time constant.
155    double p_d = Math.exp(-dt / timeConstant);
156    double p_v = Math.exp(-dt / (timeConstant / 5.0));
157    m_l1 = 1.0 + m_A - p_v - p_d;
158    m_l2 = (1.0 - p_v) * (1.0 - p_d) / m_B;
159  }
160
161  /**
162   * Constructs a DC motor bias estimator with a nominal timestep of 20 ms.
163   *
164   * @param ks The static gain in volts. This should match the feedforward's kS, or be zero if the
165   *     feedforward doesn't use one.
166   * @param kg The gravity gain in volts. This should match the feedforward's kG, or be zero if the
167   *     feedforward doesn't use one.
168   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(units/s). Must be non-negative.
169   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(units/s²). Must be non-negative. kV and kA can't both be
170   *     zero.
171   * @param timeConstant The approximate time in seconds for the input bias estimate to converge to
172   *     a new constant input bias. Must be positive.
173   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the parameter constraints are violated.
174   */
175  public DCMotorBiasEstimator(double ks, double kg, double kv, double ka, double timeConstant) {
176    this(ks, kg, kv, ka, timeConstant, 0.020);
177  }
178
179  /**
180   * Constructs a DC motor bias estimator for a mechanism without a gravity term, such as a flywheel
181   * or drivetrain, with a nominal timestep of 20 ms.
182   *
183   * <p>The model is
184   *
185   * <pre>
186   * a = −kV/kA·v + 1/kA·(u + d) − kS/kA·sgn(v)
187   * </pre>
188   *
189   * <p>where a is the acceleration, v is the velocity, u is the applied voltage, and d is the
190   * estimated input bias.
191   *
192   * @param ks The static gain in volts. This should match the feedforward's kS, or be zero if the
193   *     feedforward doesn't use one.
194   * @param kv The velocity gain in V/(units/s). Must be non-negative.
195   * @param ka The acceleration gain in V/(units/s²). Must be non-negative. kV and kA can't both be
196   *     zero.
197   * @param timeConstant The approximate time in seconds for the input bias estimate to converge to
198   *     a new constant input bias. Must be positive.
199   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the parameter constraints are violated.
200   */
201  public DCMotorBiasEstimator(double ks, double kv, double ka, double timeConstant) {
202    this(ks, 0.0, kv, ka, timeConstant, 0.020);
203  }
204
205  /**
206   * Returns the input bias estimate.
207   *
208   * @param velocity The velocity from the current timestep.
209   * @param voltage The voltage applied for the current timestep.
210   * @return The input bias estimate in volts.
211   */
212  public double calculate(double velocity, double voltage) {
213    // Voltage left over after the static friction and gravity terms
214    double u = voltage - m_ks * Math.signum(velocity) - m_kg;
215
216    double residual = velocity - m_velocity;
217    m_velocity = m_A * m_velocity + m_B * (u + m_inputBias) + m_l1 * residual;
218    m_inputBias += m_l2 * residual;
219
220    return m_inputBias;
221  }
222
223  /**
224   * Resets the estimator to the given velocity with no input bias.
225   *
226   * @param velocity The current velocity.
227   */
228  public void reset(double velocity) {
229    m_velocity = velocity;
230    m_inputBias = 0.0;
231  }
232}
